summary: Fixed the three owed findings. IN-M1 (O-045): `CommandLine.Arguments` now makes the repair only when the quotes after the program name pair up (an even count) and the repair hides no option Windows exposed (a standalone `--…` token) and no root whose only damage is a trailing quote; otherwise it falls back as for a failed alignment (argv when every quote is trailing, else null). So `D:\Data\" --report out.json` stays three arguments and runs report mode as the base did, and the `%~dp0"data"` idiom still repairs. RD-m1 (O-046/O-051): `ReportFile.Probe` opens with `FileShare.Delete` and deletes the probe by name while its handle is open, so a create-only drop folder is refused with exit 3 before any window. Both given tests are at their paths verbatim and pass, and each class has a committed corpus with the before/after measured. Whole suite 1448 of 1448 (was 1443) and the bug project 7 of 7. On the published exe the finding's line exits 0 with root `<tree>\`, and a create-only drop folder exits 3 in 186 ms with no window and nothing left.

obligations.how: CommandLineUnpairedQuoteTests passes as given (engine command run again: 1 of 1). The fix is the pairing and exposed-token steps in CommandLine.Arguments: an odd number of quotes after the program name, or a repair that would hide a standalone `--…` option or a trailing-quote root, falls back exactly as a failed alignment does. The corpus row Q01 `C:\scripts\"data" --report out.json` still gives [C:\scripts\data, --report, out.json], and Q02 does the same with a space in the name. With the fix removed, U01-U09 fail (joined into one argument, or --report hidden) and the given test fails; Q01-Q09 pass either way. A sweep of 7,380 lines holds four properties (no exposed option hidden, a repair never leaves a quote open, an exposed root never joined, null only when a quote is inside an argument). On the Debug apphost the exe fact for the unpaired line hangs 7 s without the fix and exits 0 with it. On the published exe: `<tree>\" --report <r>`, `<tree>\" --report "<r>`, the idiom `<parent>\"data" --report <r>` and the original quoted line all exit 0 in under 1.4 s with the right root.

mutation.find: return JoinsNothingWindowsSplit(argv, repaired, commandLine.AsSpan(rest).Count('"')) ? [.. repaired] : null;

obligations.how: Probe opens with Share = FileShare.Delete and calls File.Delete(probe) while the handle is held, as prescribed. ReportFileDropFolderTests passes as given (engine command run again: 1 of 1). Before the fix it fails with 'the probe passed a folder whose report the write then could not put in place'. The class corpus holds 11 folder-rights shapes: the probe is refused exactly when the write is. F03 (the create-only drop folder) is the row that failed before ('probe was ok and the write refused'), and the rest pass either way. On the published exe a create-only drop folder gives exit 3 in 186 ms, no window and an empty folder, and the Debug-apphost exe fact for it fails without the fix (window, scan, exit 3 at 1147 ms).
The same finding as O-046, answered by the same change: ReportFile.Probe's FileShare.Delete and File.Delete(probe). ReportFileDropFolderTests passes as given, and the rights corpus is the same file.

deviations: IN-M1's fix names two fallback conditions (an odd quote count, and a --report element the repair lacks). I generalised the second to a standalone token starting with `--` and added the same for a root whose only damage is a trailing quote, and put both in one predicate beside the quote count. Reason: two strays that pair (`D:\A\" D:\B\"`, or `D:\Data\" --report "out.json`) have an even count, and the first joins two roots Windows had split. Every added condition only returns a line to the base's behaviour (argv, or null), so it cannot add a hang; the idiom rows Q01 and Q02 and the finish-line rows still repair.
Added two exe-level facts to the bug project (the unpaired-quote line, and the create-only drop folder), beyond the two given unit tests, because both findings were measured at the exe.
not_built: Write still cannot remove its temporary in a create-only folder (the file inherits the Deny DELETE), as the finding notes. It is not reached there now that the probe refuses such a folder up front; the ReportFileDropFolderTests premise calls Write directly and leaves one temporary, which the test's cleanup removes.
The waived findings (O-047 and O-052 comment, O-048 program-name rule, O-049 and O-050 rule spellings) were not touched.
follow_ups: Two stray backslash-quotes with no option and an unquoted root pairing across a space (`D:\A\" D:\B\"`) now fall back to argv as the base did; a stray that pairs only inside a quoted part that has no whitespace between it and its closing quote is still repaired by design (the batch idiom).
